utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good morning to everybody in and around the courtroom. Good morning, Mr. Registrar. Will you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-81-T, the Prosecutor versus Momcilo Perisic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Could we have the appearances for the day, starting with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning, counsel. Mark Harmon, Salvatore Cannata and Carmela Javier for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Mr. Harmon. And for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in the trial against Mr. Perisic. He is represented in the courtroom today by Mr. Gregor Guy-Smith, Boris Zorko and Novak Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Mr. Lukic. Good morning to you, Mr. Borovic. I hope you have had a good rest last night. Mr. Borovic, just to remind that you are still bound by the declaration that you made at the beginning of your testimony to tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing else but the truth. Thank you so much. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, General, to you personally. Let me address you like that now. We will continue with different topics, but with the same rhythm as yesterday, please consider that you should wait a little bit with your answer after my question. We managed to be warned only once by interpreters yesterday and not a single time by the Trial Chamber, which I considered a success. Let me go back a little bit. When did you learn that the Army of Republika Srpska is to be formed?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I learned from General Djukic when he was supposed to go and hand over his duty to me, he then told me that it would be formed and that he was leaving for Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you have an occasion later on in your work to meet General Djukic?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I met him later as well. We also lived close by and he used to visit the technical administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What can you tell us about General Djukic's position about General Mladic, judging on these later occasions when you met him?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: His position was that it was very difficult to influence the General.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yesterday you told us a bit about the dislocation of the Yugoslav People's Army when it was withdrawing from the territory of Bosnia and Croatia and what were the problems which arose in connection with this withdrawal process. While you were working in the technical administration and later, what did you know about the misappropriation of materiel of the Yugoslav Army by the Army of Republika Srpska? How was that done? Was it done in an organised manner or not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So, Mr. Lukic, you are interpreted as saying "the misappropriation." Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Maybe the English word used is wrong, but simply can you tell us anything about how the materiel and technical equipment were sent to Republika Srpska during the time while you were in the technical administration?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The technical equipment and materiel was sent to the Army of Republika Srpska in two ways. One was legal and documented and the other way was illegal because the materiel withdrawn from republics that had seceded were not entered in the system of the Yugoslav Army. They were probably on the vehicles on which they had been towed. So it happened because the situation was such that the logistical structure in the technical service was dominated by people from Bosnia and Herzegovina. So sometimes they would illegally hand over technical equipment and materiel, because of this we frequently had to block off our own depots in order to prevent this misappropriation. And then there was also illegal smuggling and all kinds of channels were used. These were all difficulties for us because we were building our own service and our own army and we also had to fight all kinds of problems which arose from the war and most of them were of an illegal nature.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What sort of measures did you in the technical service take in connection with this kind of incident?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We requested assistance from security organs so that they would secure the depots and we would dismiss some of the desk clerks who allowed this kind of practice to happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What was General Perisic's position when he was assigned the Chief of General Staff of the Yugoslav Army in connection with this sort of illegal misappropriation of technical equipment and materiel?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what his position was when he was appointed to his duty, but when I came to the office he probably had not changed his position. It was that nothing should be done illegally by smuggling, by abusing assistance, but that everything should be done through legal institutions. He provided assistance to everyone who was protecting the property of the Yugoslav Army. He also issued tasks to Aco Dimitrijevic and to commanders to prevent this, and he also took measures within his remit of work directed at commanding officers who were his subordinates to stop that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a second, Judge David wants to ask you a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: General, let me go back to a question that was asked by Mr. Lukic. At page 12, lines 35, 36, it says: "When did you learn that the Army of the Republika Srpska is to be formed," and he said "when." And you said, lines 37 to 39, "I learned from General Djukic," but you didn't say when. So could you give us the dates for that question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I probably have the date somewhere in my file. I don't know the exact date, but once I received my duty in the technical service from General Djukic, that was the time. It could be specified but I don't remember the exact date. I remember that it happened and that I gave some staff equipment to the General, a ruler and something, but I don't remember when exactly that this happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we did not include the personnel file of this witness among the documents to be used because we considered that it was not relevant because he was a member of the Yugoslav Army all along, but I think I went through these dates at the beginning of my questioning. If you wish, I might present the dates to the witness as it figures in his personnel file and then he can confirm it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: Not necessary. I just wanted the witness to answer your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we please see 5628 [as interpreted], which is a Prosecution exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, we haven't reached 5000 exhibits even for the Prosecution in this trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was P628.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As we can see, this is a memo from the Chief of General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia dated the 15th of August, 1994, where he refers to his instructions from the 18th of February of the same year. And as you were still a member of the technical administration at the time, does this reflect what you advocated at the time in connection with the subject we were just discussing?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does, and there were such warnings and orders issued later as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We heard here before this Court the evidence that in early August 1994, the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia imposed an embargo on Republika Srpska. I will now ask you if you remember what was General Perisic's position and the position of the Yugoslav Army towards this embargo, generally speaking?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that the position of General Ratko Milovanovic, who was the deputy -- he was the assistant for logistics to General Perisic, that we had to honour these sanctions strictly and that we must not provoke the international community with anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And later on when you were transferred to the Chief of General Staff office, did you have an occasion to talk about this with General Perisic, so do you know what was his position beginning in December 1994 and onwards with regard to this matter?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Perisic strictly carried out the orders of the Supreme Defence Council at the time and he never issued orders to his subordinates to do anything that was not in accordance with these decisions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. General, have you heard of General Boro Ivanovic?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I heard of him and I knew General Boro Ivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Which duty was he performing in 1994?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Ivanovic was in the Novi Sad Corps. I think that he was Chief of Staff and then later on the commander of the Novi Sad Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Of which army?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Yugoslav Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm just asking you to be precise, that's all. Do you remember whether any proceedings were initiated against him in connection with the topic we are discussing right now?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that there were proceedings initiated against him. I think I was in the 1st Army at the time and that -- and that he was removed from duty at the time. I cannot remember what was the exact reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please see a document from the 65 ter Defence list, 01166D. First of all, can we turn to the next page to see who signed this document, and then we would return to the first page, if possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is a decision by which Major-General Boro Ivanovic is to face trial before the disciplinary court pursuant to a decision of the General Staff of the Yugoslav Army, Colonel-General Momcilo Perisic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now if we can please show page 1 again and you might read it for yourself, and I also invite the Trial Chamber to have a look at this document and then after a few seconds I will ask you a question about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General, the document speaks for itself. Let me ask you this: The format of this document about initiating disciplinary proceedings against him, does it have to do with what we have discussed so far?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to object to the witness testifying about this document. He testified earlier that he could not remember the reason why this individual was sanctioned. He was in the 1st Army at the time, he thinks he was removed from duty. Unless he can lay a better foundation for the use of this document, I object to the witness testifying about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one moment, please. I'm not sure that was the witness's answer and I was trying to jog the witness's memory since we showed this document to him during the proofing. And Mr. Harmon also stated his position about the document. In that regard, I wanted to ask the witness this:

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General, do you know what the reasons were to initiate this disciplinary procedure against --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Wait a minute, wait a minute, Mr. Lukic. There is an objection on the table so you don't go to the witness to address the objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I'm referring to the answer, Your Honour, that's found at page 7, line 8 through 11.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I maintain that it is my belief the witness's recollection could be jogged by this document. And perhaps now that he can see it before him, he may be able to recall the reasons as to why this disciplinary procedure was initiated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is being used to jog the witness's memory, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: That's fine. Then I withdraw my objection, but if it doesn't jog his memory, then I will re-assert my objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General, have a look at the document. Do you recall based on this document what the reasons were to initiate the disciplinary proceedings against Mr. Ivanovic?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I mentioned in my answer that I cannot recall exactly whether he was Chief of Staff or commander at the time of his removal, but in any case, he was removed because overstepped the authority to issue equipment to the VRS and the ARSK from the reserves of the VJ in contravention to the decision that existed. I know he was removed and I know what his subsequent fate was and this document dealt with the issue. I didn't see it at the time but I was familiar with that situation. I know of his removal because he overstepped his authority.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this document into evidence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I also know Colonel Miodrag Jovanovic who is referred to in the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be assigned Exhibit D480. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next document regarding this topic, since you know -- since you said that he was removed, is another 65 ter document number 01165D.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I know that document is gone, Mr. Lukic, but as it left, looking at the tables on the two languages, the language on the -- the table on the English language looked very scanty compared to the one on the other side, on the B/C/S. Not this one, the previous document, Exhibit D480. Sorry, I would like to see that again, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly. Could we please have the previous document back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Right. Now, if you look at the items that are supposed to have been disposed of in English there are so few, and in the B/C/S the table is huge. I would like to have a fuller table of the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think we have a full translation, as far as I can see. If you look at the dots in the B/C/S, they are there just to mark the space between the type of equipment and the number of pieces. In the English, these items are simply brought closer. There are no dots, but the rest corresponds. This is actually the official translation of the CLSS. The only thing missing is that right after the number it doesn't say "pieces" which is something there is in the B/C/S. The rest, I believe, fully corresponds to the B/C/S version. If you compare the numbers, you'll be able to see that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic. We had only been shown the first page of the English and I didn't see the second page.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Apologies, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You can go to your next document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next document, as I said, is 65 ter 01165D.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Before us is a presidential decree issued by the FRY president dated the 2nd August 1994. If we look down the page, we see that it was signed for the president by whom?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is General Perisic's signature. He could sign this decree on behalf of the FRY president. So the decree was proposed by the Chief of General Staff and the FRY president could accept or reject, and General Perisic signed this as part of his own remit.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you just repeat the last part of your sentence.

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the presidential decree was accepted and under his authority, the Chief of General Staff signed this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you something else. You described yesterday your contacts with Mr. Milosevic. What could you tell us about the amount and type of information Mr. Milosevic received from VJ generals?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: President Milosevic knew personally all VJ generals, but he didn't treat all of them equally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The witness is not answering your question. And I'm not quite sure whether the question you put is what you want to ask. "What could you tell us about the amount and type of information Mr. Milosevic received from VJ generals?" That's a huge question. I don't know whether anybody -- I don't know whether Mr. Milosevic can answer that question himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll be more precise, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: To the best of your recollection and the information you had, did Mr. Milosevic know all VJ generals in terms of being familiar with their background and professionalism?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: President Milosevic knew all VJ generals because he was in charge of their promotion. He had his own information and his own opinion of them and he also received information from them as he did from other services.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did he have the same position vis-a-vis all VJ generals?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: President Milosevic did not have the same position towards all generals of the VJ. He seemed to respect more those generals who were inclined towards his line of policy and his own party than those who were simply professionals.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We could see in this document that in August 1994 General Ivanovic was removed from duty. Do you know what happened with him later on as part of the disciplinary procedure initiated?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that he was placed in another position and promoted.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: By whose decision?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, only the Supreme Defence Council could decide on generals promotion, and although I cannot say precisely, but I presume that it was President Milosevic's decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I'm going to object to that. It is his speculation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think this is speculation. He told us what the extent of his knowledge is about the way generals are promoted.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am objecting to the speculation that "I presume it was Milosevic's decision." I think that's speculation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will not put any further questions in that vein.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it definitely was not President Djukanovic's decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Borovic, the procedure here is, when you see counsel for the Prosecution standing up and objecting, you keep quiet. Okay? You don't say one word until we come back to you. Okay. Yes, Mr. Lukic, the witness said "I presume."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I won't put any further questions in that vein. I just wanted to know whose decision it was formally speaking. Officially speaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did General Perisic express his position to you about this disciplinary procedure against Ivanovic and after the Supreme Defence Council decision?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall having spoken with General Perisic about this topic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this document into evidence, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be assigned Exhibit D481. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General, have you heard of the 30th and 40th Personnel Centres?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Have you ever seen the documents establishing these personnel centres while you were in your various duties with the VJ?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have. I have seen the documents about the establishment and functioning of personnel centres.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In your view or in your knowledge, what was the job of the 30th and 40th Personnel Centres?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were administrative bodies under the personnel administration which were established to keep registers and deal with the status of those officers who were with the VRS and the ARSK. And they were later on sent as volunteers to these two armed forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: While you were in the office as Chef de Cabinet, did you have any contact with the 30th and 40th Personnel Centres of the VJ?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not have any contact. There was no working relationship and there was no connection in terms of hierarchy between the personnel centres and our administration. I did have contact with the personnel administration, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If some material had to be prepared for a session of the Supreme Defence Council that had to do with those officers who belonged to the 30th and 40th Personnel Centres, who was in charge of preparing that material for the Chief of General Staff?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All material for the Supreme Defence Council which had to do with personnel issues was prepared by the sector for manning and mobilisation. That is to say, by General Matovic. That kind of material did not go through the office.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Does it also include promotions of VJ generals?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It also included promotions of VJ generals. For us it was a secret because all of us who were in the office were of junior ranks to those proposed for promotion.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What are the tasks of the office of the Chief of the General Staff in preparing a session of the Supreme Defence Council? What does the office do?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The office prepared a plan of presentations, visual presentations to be made by the Chief of the General Staff at a Supreme Defence Council session, for instance. As for documents and background material that was prepared by assistants according to their various departments.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just be more precise when you say "assistants"?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Assistant for personnel, Mr. -- General Matovic, General Martinovic would be assistant for general affairs, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Those would be chiefs of sectors?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they would be chiefs of sectors and at the same time assistants to the Chief of General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you ever attend a session of the Supreme Defence Council?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the extent I can remember now, I attended only one that was held at the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When, if you can remember? At the time General Perisic was the chief, during your tenure as Chef de Cabinet or later?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that was when I served in the office. It was a conference hall in the General Staff headquarters. You could look at the minutes to see which session it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Where were Supreme Defence Council sessions normally held?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sessions of the Supreme Defence Council, the VSO, were normally held in a villa in a neighbourhood of Belgrade called Senjak or another neighbourhood called Dedinje. Sometimes they were held in the former building of the federal government which held the office of the president of Yugoslavia, Mr. Lilic. And exceptionally they would be held in the office of the Chief of General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember how many times VSO sessions were held in the General Staff headquarters?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the extent I can remember now, I think during my tenure it happened twice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What do you mean by "VSO," Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: SDC, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Supreme Defence Council.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did the office of the Chief of General Staff later receive minutes from Supreme Defence Council sessions?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The VSO is the Supreme Defence Council and their decisions and minutes would not be passed on to the office of the Chief of General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You told us yesterday you lecture on a subject called the theory of decision-making. Tell me, what importance do decisions of the Supreme Defence Council have for the office of the Chief of the General Staff?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Chief of the General Staff has to implement decisions of the Supreme Defence Council in the best possible way.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let's move to a different subject. Did the office receive requests from the Army of Republika Srpska, the Army of the RSK, the governments of the RSK and Republika Srpska for material assistance? Did these requests pass through the office of the Chief of General Staff?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Requests coming from the General Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska did pass through and were supposed to pass through our office. Requests from the ministries of these republics were supposed to pass through our office to the minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Which office?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The office of the defence minister of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What is the procedure normally when you receive such a request from, let's say, the General Staff of the VRS, the Army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the office we would study the request, see what kind of request it was, and depending on whose jurisdiction, whose purview it was along tactical lines, we would pass it to the General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia for them to assess their own abilities to assist. And then they were supposed to suggest a certain position or a certain decision to the Chief of the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Before we go on, to the best of your knowledge, what elements would be taken into account by the tactical decision-makers when they assess a request?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first criterion would be to what extent granting such assistance would lessen the combat readiness of the Army of Yugoslavia. Whether the assets required would be from surpluses and reserves or they would be from the currently used assets of the VJ. And since we had quotas for everything, they would assess to what extent the request was justified by the assignment, the mission cited in the document, because it was thought that the organs of these two armies did not know the situation on the ground very well and did not know the status of their own reserves and supplies very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What kind of information did you in the VJ have about that? Could you just answer the question that I just asked more precisely. When you say that there was an opinion that the organs of these two armies did not know the situation on the ground very well, and they did not know the status of their own reserves very well, what do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you could see from the documents that it was a simple summing up of their own requests, a wish list practically.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Go on, what was the procedure when an assessment is received, an opinion?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, on a request sometimes several tactical decision-makers have to state their opinion depending on their responsibilities concerning various points of the request. We always wanted everyone to give us their opinion on the request depending on which sector they were covering. Then we worked on it within our office and submitted it to the Chief of General Staff for him to make a decision. If he was the one who is supposed to sign it, he would. And sometimes he would ask the Supreme Defence Council to give a final answer to the Army of Republika Srpska or the Army of the Republic of Serbian Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In practice, while you were Chef de Cabinet, did it ever happen that General Perisic approved something against a negative suggestion of the tactical sector in charge of that area?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because General Perisic was not aware of the situation in various tactical sectors on each and every issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to look at several documents now. First of all P2733. This document has several pages. We'll take it step by step. First of all, if we could see the lower part of the document, I'm interested in the format.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What type of document is this?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is standard procedure that the office implemented when receiving a request, in this case from the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What about this bit below?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since they wanted a self-propelled battery for anti-aircraft defence, we submitted it to the anti-aircraft defence sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I have the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There's something written here in longhand in the upper right corner. If you could read it, what does it say, and if you know, who wrote this?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know both.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When it arrived at the desk of the sector in charge, and that was the administration for anti-aircraft defence, the chief of that administration, Dusan Banjac, said, "I suggest that it be the self-propelled rocket battery KUB."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And what does it say above?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the administration for air force and anti-aircraft defence, urgent. Mr. Vucinic wanted his own administration to urgently provide him with an answer, their position on this request.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, I'd like a Defence exhibit from the 65 ter list, 01074D. It's the same document we've just seen. Let's see now the second page, B/C/S and English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now, what is this?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the reply from the sector chief, General Vucinic, assistant for air force and anti-aircraft defence in the General Staff. They are saying that the aircraft defence sector has these two batteries and can make them available but they are putting it to the General Staff to decide, because I know that normally they never made available to third parties complete units and complete establishment assets.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What is the decision of the collegium ultimately?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that this did not happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I tender this document, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be assigned Exhibit D482. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now have on the screen P2753. It's also on several pages. We'll go through it quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What are we looking at now?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we can again see the bottom part of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's a request from General Gvero, who was Assistant Chief of Staff for morale and information in the Army of Republika Srpska, asking for an interview to be granted to their chief with the media. The office passed this to the administration for morale and information of the General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We'll continue with the document, just let me ask you, you said Krivosija?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Krivosija was ordered to settle this with Radio Television Serbia, so the office doesn't have to deal with it anymore. Krivosija was in charge of contacts with Radio Television Serbia which was then managed by Vucelic. It was not the job of the office to deal with this anyway.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Take it slowly. Who is Vucelic?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: General director of Radio Television Serbia, or Radio Television Belgrade, if you like.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And who was Krivosija at the time?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the president of the military office of the FRY president, Lilic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you remember as this is a document from August 1995, I will not go into details, but just what it says here. In the RS, information blockade has been imposed on the members of the VRS. Do you remember what was the occasion for this?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a conflict between the military and political leaderships of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now please see the fourth page of this document in the B/C/S version. I'm not sure of the English version, let me just see. It's the response by General Krivosija. Here it is on the screen, we can see it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Once again the document speaks for itself. Who would this document be forwarded to?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then one should respond to Gvero, but considering the contents of the document, if there was a response, it would be sent to Gvero.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please see page 3 of this document. I mean in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, here we see that General Gvero was informed about the possibilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And from the correspondence which we have seen in this document, what was the position of the General Staff?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is where the role of the General Staff ends. We informed everyone about what was possible and the office of the Chief of General Staff was not following this anymore. The procedure had been completed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did General Perisic take any decision or have any role in the decisions pertaining to these requests?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he did not play any role in this and he wasn't supposed to.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you possibly know whether this was really done later on? Was there a general -- was there an interview with General Mladic that was broadcast by the RTS?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please see the next P exhibit -- no, I'm sorry, this is a document from the 65 ter Defence list, 1055D.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us briefly what this document refers to?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is a response of the Ministry of Defence of Republika Srpska Krajina. They first asked for concrete elements for blocking roads to be given to them, made of reinforced concrete and also some quantities of mines and explosives that would be used for blocking certain roads in the area of Slavonia and Baranja. This is the final document in which the office informed the ministry that such reinforced concrete elements were produced by our military construction institution from Kraljevo which is a military profit-making institution and could produce these sets for them at a certain cost, which is mentioned here. And those who were in charge were -- had probably assigned a certain number of mines and explosives to be used for blocking possible access that would be used for attack against the Army of Republic of Serbian Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I seek to tender this document into evidence, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be assigned Exhibit D483. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now please see another document from the Defence 65 ter list, 00847D.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Once again, General, could you please comment on this document.

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Main Staff of the Army of the Serbian Krajina requested jet fuel GM-1. It was a problem for army to this day and we informed them here that the army could not resolve that, that they had to resolve it by requesting from the leadership of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, the oil refinery, and other organs to do this. And they never replied to that and they never even had jet fuel.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, I seek to tender this document into evidence as well, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be assigned Exhibit D484. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please see P2746, which is a Prosecution exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will show you another document and then I will ask you for additional answers. What I'm interested in right now is just a form of this request and what would happen with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please show the bottom of this document on the screen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was a request we received from the Main Staff and they were asked for contact fuse aerial bombs. It was immediately sent to the air force and anti-aircraft defence to resolve it and to send feedback to the office.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the upper part it says: "In order to repossess the lost facilities in the ZOHK," what is that?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the zone of responsibility of the Herzegovina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please see another document on the screen, namely P951. Another Prosecution exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Could we just repeat the number of the exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] P951. We can see it on the screen now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General, what can we see now?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is an information that this has been approved of, the collection of these from the 608th Logistics Base, it's a logistics base of the Supreme Command.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I want to ask you the following now: This was in October 1995, what do you remember about what was happening at the time in the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, the Herzegovina Corps had lost some positions and wanted to retake them before the cessation of hostilities would come into place. This is why they wanted to do it. But I think that the operational reports contained a description of the entire situation. I don't remember the details right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were you receiving any information during the war that aerial bombs were used by members of the Army of Republika Srpska in order to target facilities in the city of Sarajevo or against other civilian targets?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We never received information that aerial bombs were used in order to attack populated places.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll move to the next document now. It's an exhibit of the Defence, D172.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is a document from November 1994, and we can see that the Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Serbian Krajina sent a letter to the Ministry of Defence of FR Yugoslavia requesting certain ammunition. Can you just tell us, these shells which are listed here, were these shells to be used in offensive or defensive operations, if you know?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are shells for mortars, MB-60 and MB-82, these are the millimetre calibres, and that's a weapon that the infantry has.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And it says here that they should be sent without anything being paid for them?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are asking for that because one ministry is selling it to another. They are selling something that the military production facilities are making.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now see another document. It's another Prosecution exhibit, P1142.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It says here in this document, a memo from the Ministry of Defence sent to the office of the Chief of the General Staff of the Yugoslav Army and there's something written by hand at the top of the page, and whose handwriting is it?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the handwriting of General Momcilo Perisic and it says, "Not without the Supreme Defence Council."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please see 1143 -- I apologise, P1143, a Prosecution exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you please comment on this document for us, General?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a standard document. It's a response to the office of the federal Ministry of Defence, namely that the chief decided that he would not issue any materiel without the decision of the Supreme Defence Council, and that the minister, because he was a member of Supreme Defence Council, should place this document on the agenda of the Supreme Defence Council.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Slow down, Mr. Borovic, the interpreter was desperately trying --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just to specify something, you said that the minister is a member of the Supreme Defence Council. So let me ask you first of all, who were, as far as remember, the members of the Supreme Defence Council?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The members of the Supreme Defence Council were the president of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, Mr. Zoran Lilic; the president of the Republic of Serbia, Slobodan Milosevic; and the president of the Republic of Montenegro, Momir Bulatovic, and later on he was succeeded by Milo Djukanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As far as you know, who regularly attending the meetings of the Supreme Defence Council?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Members regularly attended it as well as the Chief of the General Staff, the chief of the military office and very frequently the federal prime minister, Mr. Kontic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How about the minister of defence?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the minister of defence as well, he was a member of the Supreme Defence Council, and Mr. Kontic often attended it as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was the minister of defence of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia a member or did he just attend these meetings?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The minister was a member of the Supreme Defence Council.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it's time for the break, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is indeed. We'll take a break and come back at quarter to 11.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have 65 ter document 02177D.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General, can you briefly comment on this document?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the reply to the General Staff of the RS specifying that the army is unable to deliver the assets they requested.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this document into evidence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be assigned Exhibit D485. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next document --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Just one intervention for purposes of the record. I'm referring to General's answer found at page 29, line 1, where he says this is a reply to the General Staff of the RS. The face of the document doesn't indicate this is from the RS. The face of the document reflects this is the Main Staff -- directed to the Main Staff of the Army of the Serbian Krajina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you for the correction, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Prosecution Exhibit P2726. I need the upper part of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could we please have that on the screen. There is a handwritten note, General, on this document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I do not have a copy of this document. It was not notified to me and I'm wondering if counsel has a copy of an English version of this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise again if we omitted it from the list. Unfortunately, I do not have an English copy. I made copies for myself only, but we have the English translation on the screen. It is a Prosecution exhibit and I believe Mr. Harmon used it a number of times. I am being told by Mr. Zorko that it is on the list actually. The Prosecution was notified. And we are in the process of printing it out. The Registrar is doing that and we'll have a copy for Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The handwritten remark on the document, can you tell us what this says and whose handwriting it is?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a request of the Main Staff of the VRS to the chief of the General Staff of the VJ. We see General Perisic's handwriting. It says: "Give it to Ratko to deal with it, Momcilo Perisic."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we go to the end of the document in both versions. The bottom part. Could we please zoom in on the bottom part in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you read this out?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already have.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who is this document addressed to, as we see in the bottom part?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It said before that it should be given to Ratko to deal with it, and we sent it to lieutenant -- Colonel-General Ratko Mladenovic [as interpreted] to deal with it, to provide his opinion and this was sent by my deputy, Vlajkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We are finished with this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can we just -- can the record just indicate that it is not Mladenovic. It is Milovanovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we next have 65 ter document 10085D [as interpreted]. I notified Mr. Harmon yesterday about my intention to use this document with the witness. I didn't even show it to the witness during proofing. I showed him another document and I just wanted to link it up to this one.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Could the counsel please repeat the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. 65 ter 01085D.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, since you have never seen this document before, please read it slowly to yourself. It is document number 04/9-10 of the 4th September 1995. What is this Silo asset?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is an anti-aircraft weapon system to engage low-flying airplanes. It is a rocket launched from the ground. It is stated here that that asset proved inefficient and they wanted to receive better assets from our command.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What about the handwritten note, can you tell us what it says and whose handwriting it is?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is the handwriting of the late General Mirko Vucinic, who was assistant to the Chief of the General Staff for the air force and anti-aircraft defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have an exhibit number for this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be assigned Exhibit D486. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what the position was of the commander?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of the air force and anti-aircraft defence was of the position that those assets should not be provided. He invoked a decision of the Chief of the General Staff he refers to in the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we next have 65 ter document 01062D.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: A moment ago I stated what the number of the document was in the previous exhibit, the document number, and in view of that, what can you tell us about this document, vis-a-vis the previous request we saw?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the reply of the office to the Main Staff of the RS. We tell them that we were not in a position to secure the requested anti-aircraft assets.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we also get an exhibit number for this document, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Its admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be assigned Exhibit D487. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Next document is 65 ter number -- it will be the last document about this topic. The number is 01049D.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General, could you please comment on this document?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is a reply to the request to have flame-throwers issued. The VJ and our office advised that we were not in a position to send them the requested flame-throwers because even the ones we had did not have ignition cartridges.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this document as well, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Its admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be assigned Exhibit D488. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please now analyse two Prosecution exhibits next. It is P2727 to start with. When analysing this document, I'd like to go in chronological order. So let's start with page 3 in e-court in the Serbian version. I am just checking whether it's the same page in the English. That is not the page. Yes, this is it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The bureau of Republika Srpska, which was a governmental organ of theirs in Belgrade, they are addressing the federal Ministry of Defence of the FRY, requesting that they be provided with stationary and mobile radio sets as specified further below.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's look at page 2 in the B/C/S in e-court. And we'll be able to locate the English page afterwards. 6775ET, that should be the English page.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm interested in what this is. What is this that we see on the screen concerning the request?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the office of the federal Ministry of Defence, once they had studied the request, they sent it to the office of the Chief of the General Staff. They forwarded this request for the issue of Motorola stations, radio stations, and an answer was sent to the sector for communications, information technologies, and electronic operations, or actually, it was forwarded to the sector asking for their position.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we go to page 4 in the English. Actually, it is page 4 in the B/C/S and the English page should be 6778ET. Sorry, it's actually page 5. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What is this?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an answer from the chief of communications sector of electronic and anti-electronic combat that they are able to provide -- that they agree to purchase a number of Motorolas.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If somebody wants to purchase this type of Motorola which does not belong normally in the standard system of the Army of Yugoslavia, why are they, the General Staff of the Yugoslav Army, required to state their opinion?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Motorola devices did not belong in the standard equipment of the Yugoslav People's Army, or the Army of Republika Srpska or the Army of Yugoslavia. And when it is introduced into the communications system and when communications are established using different technology, the sector in charge must assess how appropriate these devices are and how safe it is to include them in the communications system, the level where these devices can be used, and they are providing a technical opinion whether this fits into the communications system or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I meant to ask something slightly different. When somebody else want to buy Motorolas that don't belong in the standard equipment of the VJ, could it pose a problem to the Army of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they were not part of system of the Army of Republika Srpska either, but since they were communications between the Army of Republika Srpska and the Army of Yugoslavia using devices made by same producers, they were asking whether this could pose a threat to the communications system of the Army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's now complete, I mean your answer on the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see page 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What is this and to whom are you writing?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We are writing to the office of the federal defence minister saying that our sector in charge of these matters believe that these devices may be used and then the federal defence ministry is suppose to present this to the federal minister or the Supreme Defence Council.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll now review another Prosecution exhibit, P2728. We could start with page 3 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let's begin with the request. What is being requested, by whom and from whom?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Republika Srpska, the defence ministry, is addressing the defence ministry of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia requesting technical documentation for the production of ammunition for submachine-gun Browning, for a submachine-gun DSK, and 82-millimetre shells with aluminium stabiliser or mines, because that technical documentation was kept by the federal defence ministry of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll skip one document because the procedure is similar and let's look at page 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What is this?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This went to the chief of the technical administration, the logistical sector, General Kodzopeljic, but he answered, it's not in their jurisdiction. It was the jurisdiction of the sector for research and production of military assets. This technical documentation was developed by the Military Technical Institute. His position briefly is that this documentation may be made available but it's up to the federal minister to decide. It's, by the way, a document that should never have appeared.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now let's move to a Prosecution exhibit, P720. I don't know if this is under seal. These are minutes from a Supreme Defence Council session. 38th session of the SDC.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Were they not under seal or have they been lifted?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm told the seal was removed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic. You may proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We see that these are the minutes from the 38th session of the Supreme Defence Council held on 27 June 1995. We should move to page 3 in B/C/S and in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We should look at item 4, the third entry under item 4. We see that the president, Zoran Lilic, suggests that three issues be reviewed. And under 2 it says: "Requests from Republika Srpska for assistance in equipping the Special Police Brigade purchasing Motorola radios and obtaining a copy of the technical documentation for the manufacturing of ammunition." Right?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now we need the last page in B/C/S and in English with the decisions of the Supreme Defence Council. I am sorry, we need to see the previous page in English as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'll read item 2: "With regard to the requests received from Republika Srpska, the Supreme Defence Council stands by its earlier decisions." From these documents we've been looking at recently, the three or five exhibits, the requests from Republika Srpska, who made the decisions? Who had a say in whether they would be granted or not?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Supreme Defence Council decided and since we see that Major-General Slavoljub Susic was present, he knew about these decisions and that's why it says "stands by its earlier decisions."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I'd like to move to another area. I am done with the logistics. Court's indulgence for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's page 36, line 13, in the transcript, you mentioned that decision was signed by General Jugoslav, what is the last name?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kodzopeljic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: To whom was the Technical Military Institute subordinated?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the administration for research, development, and production of military equipment. It was under the defence ministry, the federal defence ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now call up - moving to another subject - P2751. These would be documents from the office of the Chief of General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is a document that the office of the Chief of the General Staff sent to the military office of the president of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's move to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You've seen this document in proofing, and tell us what this is about.

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It must be the office of the president of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia that asked us to produce criteria according which the Ministry of the Interior of the Republika Srpska was sending volunteers to the Republika Srpska and the Republic of Serbian Krajina. Our office tried using regular channels to obtain these criteria used by the Ministry of the Interior and we got them. Here in the subheading it says according to our unofficial information from employees of the Ministry of the Interior. These are the criteria listed here, based on which the Ministry of the Interior was sending volunteers and natives of Croatia and Bosnia to the theatre of war.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the next page, please. B/C/S and English.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm a bit confused by the witness's evidence because he refers to volunteers and this document doesn't address the issue of volunteers on its face. It deals with the sending of military conscripts, not volunteers, so perhaps Mr. Lukic can have the witness direct us to that portion of this document where there's a reference to volunteers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: First of all, I'll ask the witness if he was the author of this document?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am because I signed it and I sent it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And now having heard the objection by Mr. Harmon, can you tell us from your memory to whom this document applied? Why did President Lilic ask you for this information in the first place?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember what exactly was the reason, but I know that at that time only volunteers were being sent. The Ministry of the Interior equipped them, rallied them according to certain criteria. The army wasn't involved at the time. And here in the second part we also suggested to the federal president that he should present the Ministry of the Interior with our positions regarding the criteria for sending people there that had nothing to do with the Army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I still --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Borovic -- can I just hold you a little bit, Mr. Harmon. Mr. Borovic, can you read in the B/C/S the word that connotes "volunteers." Let the interpreters interpret it to us from this document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, could you go back to the first page and then I'll see. I apologise, volunteers are not mentioned here. There is a reference instead to military conscripts and that's the term used in the document, military conscripts sent to Republika Srpska and the Republic of Serbian Krajina. And according to their records, the military conscripts were those who originated from Republika Srpska and the Republic of Serbian Krajina, and they made those lists available to the Ministry of the Interior so that the MUP should send these people to Republika Srpska and Republic of Serbian Krajina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Borovic. So the document talks about conscripts. Are you clear, Mr. Harmon?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You are welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let's just look at the final part of this document, bearing in mind this is a proposal from the General Staff of the VJ. And my question is: Do you recall that the MUP rallied military conscripts from Republika Srpska and the Republic of Serbian Krajina by force and returned them to their republics to training centres? Do you remember some scandals involving that?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall anything officially, but from everything we discussed, yes, there were stories like that going around.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now, your suggestions here that you sent to the office of the supreme commander, how were they motivated?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We sent a supplement to these criteria saying that the MUP should not send military conscripts and non-commissioned officers who had an obligation to the Army of Yugoslavia and belonged to the VJ establishment, although they were military conscripts elsewhere because it would disrupt the combat readiness of the Army of Yugoslavia. And we also included in our proposal more humane treatment of family members, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at P2729.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General, just briefly about this document, are you aware that any volunteers headed by Colonel Trkulja were sent as well as a battalion by the General Staff of the Yugoslav Army? Did the Yugoslav Army General Staff act in accordance with this?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that it did and if such a unit with such a number of men was indeed sent there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If such a unit with such a number of men was sent there, would you have had to be informed about it as Chef de Cabinet?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't have had to be informed but through the office we would have arrived -- we would have received some sort of information that the unit arrive there, that it was deployed, so there would have to be final documents suggesting that this was indeed implemented.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I will move to a different topic now. Do you know whether the Yugoslav Army sent fuel to the Army of Republika Srpska and the Serbian Army of Krajina, fuel from its depots?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Supplying the Army of Republika Srpska and the Army of Republic of Serbian Krajina with fuel in an organised manner was not something that was carried out. It's possible that there may have been certain fuel trucks that were sent there because the levels of fuel were critical even within Yugoslavia and some quantities were also taken from us to be used in the agricultural works, so that we were also short of fuel.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see on the screen document P1178.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What can we see here? What is this document about?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document, signed by the previous Chef de Cabinet from whom I had taken over the duty, says that people coming officially from Republika Srpska could fill their tanks at certain gas station, 25 litres of fuel for persons who had arrived to the Republic of Serbia on duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Whose petrol stations were these?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as soon as this was issued it means that it referred to a petrol station of the Yugoslav Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were these petrol stations of the Yugoslav Army used to issue fuel for military needs in addition to tanks being filled on an individual basis as set out in this document?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Fuel for military needs would not be sent for such petrol stations. It was just -- they were just used to fill the tanks of vehicles that were passing through.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please see P2519, another Prosecution exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We can see this is another memo from the Army of Republika Srpska. Something is handwritten in the upper right-hand corner, can you tell us what it is and whose handwriting it is?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a request that two officers from the intelligence administration --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. The question has not been answered. It's non-responsive. He was asked a question as to identifying the handwriting and he is not answering the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that Mr. Harmon is too fast now. I think the witness is providing this as an introduction for his answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wanted to say that it says here Krga.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It does, we do understand that you do want to give an introduction, Mr. Borovic, but this is something that this Chamber has been raising with many witnesses. It would be very helpful if you could listen very carefully to the question and answer directly the question. If any background information is necessary, you will be asked to provide it. But try to, if you are asked whose handwriting this is, just tell us whose handwriting it is. We can see the document and read what this document is all about, so I urge you to try and be concise.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General, will you please answer the question, whose handwriting is this in the upper right-hand side corner?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is General Perisic's handwriting and it says there "Krga proposal but after discussion with them."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What does that mean? What was Krga's task judging by this document, and what does it mean after a discussion with him?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It means that Krga should not send them or write a proposal for the chief to send them, but first conduct an official interview with them, see whether they accept to be sent to carry out such a task, and then after that, submit a proposal to the Chief of General Staff. And this is what we wrote down below, to the 2nd administration, we submit a telegram and so on, just as it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Were you aware whether such persons were sent there at the request of the Army of Republika Srpska if they did not wish to go?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No one was sent by force if they did not accept this sort of task.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now we'll go back to the chronology of events and the context. General, do you know anything about people from the area of Zepa swimming across the Drina River in early August 1995, and if so, what do you know about this?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is well known that the border units of the Uzice Corps reported during the night several hundred Muslim refugees had swam over the Drina River and crossed over to our side, that the border units received them and General Disovic informed the Chief of General Staff about the incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know what the Chief of General Staff did then in connection with that? What was his reaction like?

utterances.speaker: SINISA BOROVIC [Resumed]
